t: Ipso Facto Optimism: Why We're Still Here to Argue About the End of the World
s: This technical journal excerpt argues for optimism by reframing humanity's chaotic nature as a strength, drawing parallels between abiogenesis research (Miller-Urey, protocells) and historical scientific paradigm shifts, and inverting dystopian sci-fi narratives.
sub: Abiogenesis research: From Miller-Urey experiment to modern protocells demonstrating self-assembly and early metabolism.
Historical scientific analogies: The 'two clouds' (aether and black-body radiation) as a metaphor for unexplored frontiers in biology.
Inversion of dystopian narratives: Humanity's potential as the 'apex predator' due to early AI development, challenging conventional sci-fi fears.
